I’m going to land this in coherent layers:

1. Refactor the AJC roadmap into a single nested critical path, correct contradictory statuses, and split the open flat-base-change work into explicit leaves.
2. Clean the worst blueprint journal residue in a focused chapter while preserving every mathematical node and dependency.
3. Make one measured Čech code optimization, using Lean’s profiler/min-import tooling rather than changing heartbeat values blindly.
4. Sync the graph, build the affected artifacts, obtain fresh review and janitor checks, then commit each layer separately.

This will not pretend the whole long-running project is “optimized” in one pass; it will leave the task open with a much clearer next optimization queue.
